title: untitled spatial correlation implementation
text: usci computes spatial correlation metric c two observations sets, observation value set spatial coordinates, defined : c =     \sqrt{N_A} * \sqrt{N_B} *     \frac{         \sum_{\} \sum_{j \B} (             e^{\frac{-d(, j)}{s}} *             (A_i - \overline{}) *             (B_j - \overline{B})         )      }{         (\sum_{\} \sum_{j \B} e^{\frac{-d(, j)}{s}}) *         \sqrt{\sum_{\} A_i} *         \sqrt{\sum_{j \B} B_j}     } : N_A represents size observation set d(, j) represents euclidean distance observations j A_i represents value observation observation set \overline{} represents mean value across values observation set s represents scale factor

title: untitled spatial correlation implementation
text: definition c, can see computing c O(N_A * N_B), e.g. quadratic total input size. , usci package also provides asci function, attempts return approximation c , observation , evaluating values observations B s.t. spatial weight term e^{\frac{-d(, j)}{s}} \geq \epsilon (\epsilon allowed error term, default set 1e-8). reformulating bound, see can rephrased d(, j) \leq -ln(\epsilon) * s, meaning heavily depends value scale factor. scale factor values bound allows excluding nontrivial fraction observations, allows order magnitude speed runtime causing marginal drift accuracy. using asci requires first computing spatial index observation set B, via provided build_index function.

title: untitled spatial correlation implementation
text: demonstration package use can seen :
code: library(usci)  a_n <- 128 b_n <- 256  a <- rpois(a_n, runif(1, 0, 32)) a_x <- rnorm(a_n) a_y <- rnorm(a_n)  b <- rpois(b_n, runif(1, 0, 32)) b_x <- rnorm(b_n) b_y <- rnorm(b_n)  c <- usci(a, b, a_x, a_y, b_x, b_y, 1e-1)  b_idx <- build_index(b_x, b_y) c_approx <- asci(a, b, a_x, a_y, b_idx, 1e-1)
